priogridR

priogridR provides a consistent interface for working with PRIO-GRID data. It combines grid utilities with general converters that transfer raster, vector, point-event, NetCDF, and geographically indexed tabular data to a configurable PRIO-GRID. It also supports coordinate lookup, geometry creation, spatial neighborhoods, weights, lags, distances and buffer summaries, panel validation and completion, safe joins, and rapid mapping.

The package builds on the official priogrid package for grid definitions and raster transformations.

Installation

The package is under active development and is not yet available from CRAN. Install the development version from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("christianoswald/priogridR")

Public interface

All user-facing functions begin with pg_ and use snake case:

  • pg_from_raster() converts raster layers.
  • pg_from_vector() converts point, line, or polygon features.
  • pg_from_points() is a convenience wrapper for event or coordinate data.
  • pg_from_netcdf() converts NetCDF variables and layers.
  • pg_from_table() transfers geographically indexed tabular data.
  • pg_create_indices() creates PRIO-GRID identifier matrices.
  • pg_id_from_coords() and pg_coords_from_id() convert between locations and cell identifiers.
  • pg_geometry() creates cell polygons or centre points.
  • pg_neighbors() returns first-order neighboring cells.
  • pg_neighbor_table() creates reusable contiguity, distance-band, or nearest-neighbor relationships.
  • pg_weights() constructs binary or inverse-distance spatial weights.
  • pg_spatial_lag() calculates weighted neighboring-cell values.
  • pg_distance(), pg_buffer_summary(), and pg_nearest() support common spatial-context workflows.
  • pg_validate_data() checks cell and panel structure.
  • pg_complete_panel() creates complete cell or cell-time panels.
  • pg_join() performs relationship-checked joins.
  • pg_plot() maps cell-level variables.
  • pg_paths() constructs reproducible project paths.
  • pg_theme() supplies a map-oriented ggplot2 theme.
  • pg_write_result() writes conversion outputs.

Example 

library(priogridR)

pg_create_indices(nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
##      [,1] [,2] [,3]
## [1,]    7    8    9
## [2,]    4    5    6
## [3,]    1    2    3
pg_neighbors(5, nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
## [1] 7 8 9 4 6 1 2 3

Point-event data can be aggregated using the temporal and spatial settings in a PRIO-GRID configuration:

events <- data.frame(
  longitude = c(10, 10.1, 20),
  latitude = c(50, 50.1, 60),
  event_date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-03-01", "2021-06-01"))
)

config <- priogrid::pg_config(
  temporal_resolution = "1 year",
  start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),
  end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31")
)

event_counts <- pg_from_points(
  x = events,
  variable = "event_count",
  longitude = "longitude",
  latitude = "latitude",
  aggregation = "count",
  time_column = "event_date",
  config = config
)

See vignette("getting-started", package = "priogridR") and vignette("conversion-workflows", package = "priogridR") for an introduction and a guide to choosing a converter. The package website also provides a focused article for every pg_from_*() function.

Package direction

Future convenience functions will build on the same principles: reproducible inputs, explicit spatial and temporal configurations, transparent transformations, and outputs that fit ordinary R workflows. The aim is to reduce recurring data-management and spatial-processing work for PRIO-GRID users while keeping aggregation rules, missing-data decisions, neighborhood definitions, and other analytical choices visible and under the researcher’s control.

Development will continue to complement the official priogrid package rather than duplicate its data-access, configuration, metadata, and citation infrastructure.

AI-assisted development

This package has been developed with assistance from OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Codex. AI tools have been used to support code drafting and refactoring, test development, documentation, troubleshooting, literature review, and discussion of package design.

All substantive design decisions, review of generated material, package testing, and responsibility for the correctness and maintenance of priogridR remain with the package author. AI-assisted contributions are reviewed and validated through the package’s test suite, examples, vignettes, continuous-integration workflows, and R CMD check before release.

Scope and attribution

priogridR is an independent community package. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO) or the developers of the official priogrid package.

The bundled priogrid data object contains PRIO-GRID cell identifiers, coordinates, and geometries derived from the PRIO-GRID dataset and is made available under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By) 1.0. Other data accessed, converted, or analyzed with priogridR remain subject to their original providers’ licenses, documentation, citation requirements, and terms of use.

Users should cite the original PRIO-GRID publication and all underlying data sources relevant to their analyses. The citation and licensing information provided by the official priogrid package remains authoritative for official PRIO-GRID variables and source datasets.
